key_insight: WorldDirector separates motion control from pixel generation, enabling a video world model that can keep objects persistent and let users explore scenes from different viewpoints more freely. In simple terms, it acts like a controllable simulator that remembers dynamic objects instead of depending on continuous visual input to keep them moving.
problem_solved: Existing world models often entangle scene dynamics with rendering, making them hard to control and prone to losing motion when visual observations are missing. This paper addresses the need for persistent dynamic memory and unrestricted viewpoint navigation in generated worlds.
method: Uses an LLM to orchestrate semantic motion, including 3D trajectories and camera movements.
Decouples motion planning from visual synthesis so dynamics can persist independently of frame-by-frame observation.
Generates video/world content conditioned on the planned motions, supporting controllable scene evolution and viewpoint changes.
impact: This is useful for researchers building interactive simulators, embodied AI systems, and controllable video generation tools. It improves long-horizon consistency and user control, which are key for training, testing, and exploring AI agents in simulated environments.

paper_title: WorldDirector: Building Controllable World Simulators with Persistent Dynamic Memory
paper_authors: Hanlin Wang, Hao Ouyang, Qiuyu Wang, Wen Wang, Qingyan Bai
